key_insight: The paper introduces a differentiable thermo-structural topology optimization framework that directly accounts for nonlinear creep, enabling designs that better resist long-term permanent deformation at high temperature.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for high-temperature metal components such as turbine blades, where service life is strongly affected by creep rather than only elastic stiffness.
method: Uses the Norton creep model to represent nonlinear, history-dependent material deformation.
Solves the transient coupled thermo-structural response with a backward Euler time integration scheme over the service life.
Employs JAX automatic differentiation for adjoint-based gradients in gradient-driven topology and multi-material optimization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports canonical 2D benchmarks where the method significantly reduces permanent deformation versus elastic-only designs, plus a 3D graded-material turbine blade challenge problem.
watch_item: Creep-aware optimization is computationally demanding because it must handle nonlinear time-dependent thermo-mechanical coupling and accurate material calibration.
paper_title: Thermo-Structural Topology Optimization Considering Nonlinear Creep
